messages:
Mira: seeing a small but sustained eviction spike in us-west2 this morning, looks like packing + a new taint interaction. pods with gpu-req=1 keep bouncing and some nodes have 1-2 gpus free but not schedulable :confused:
Ashish: can you paste the scheduler logs or a sample pod event? might be the new rack-aware predicate we rolled last week.
Mira: pasting a short kubectl snapshot of pending pods + node allocs:
```
$ kubectl get pods -A -o wide | egrep 'Pending|gpu' | head -n 20
redwood-ml   train-job-98   0/1   Pending   0   3m   <none>   10.40.5.12   node-selector=gpu
redwood-ml   train-job-99   0/1   Pending   0   2m   <none>   10.40.5.13   node-selector=gpu
infra        gpu-sidecar-7  1/1   Running   0   1h   node-az1-gpu03   10.40.5.16
```
Mira: and nodes show leftover tiny fragments (0.25/1 GPU allocatable) from kube-resources and our new bandwidth isolation cgroup.
Devon: @Mira saw similar last night in eu-west. The scheduler was scoring nodes with rack affinity extremely high which blocked spread packing and caused the filler pods to get stuck. Might be that rackWeight=100 we shipped.
Ashish: that sounds right — rackWeight was increased to avoid cross-rack NVLink traffic for big batches, but small single-gpu jobs now prefer a rack even if it causes fragmentation. We can try lowering weight or adding soft-affinity.
SRE Oncall: infra-bot just flagged an autoscaler loop in the same cluster, nodes spinning up then immediately draining due to taint mismatch, producing network churn. logs: infra-bot: AUTOSCALER: scale_up group=gpu-pool-usw2 count=3 reason=unsched
Mira: the eviction spikes line up with the autoscaler churn and kubelet eviction heartbeats — when new nodes come up they get tainted for bandwidth QoS and our admission controller misclassifies some daemonset pods, causing preemptive soft-evict.
Devon: can we temporarily set rackWeight=20 and reduce bandwidth-taint duration to 30s? quick rollback to test.
Ashish: will do. Also suggest a fast patch: make the small-gpu pod predicate prefer nodes with >=0.5 free gpu rather than strict integer checks (we quantize fractional reservations). fallback will reduce islanding.
Mira: rolling rackWeight -> 20 now in canary (us-west2-a). watching for pending counts. :eyes:
(2m later)
Mira: canary looks better, pending count down from 12 -> 3, a couple moved to nodes in same AZ but different rack. no evictions in the last minute.
SRE Oncall: infra-bot: ALERT CLEARED: autoscaler-loop resolved in gpu-pool-usw2 after config change.
Devon: leaving a follow-up issue for scheduler tuning + a test for taint + autoscaler interplay. we need a unit/e2e that simulates small-job defrag with rack affinity on/off.
Ashish: logging the rollback PR and a postmortem note. will include cost impact estimate (extra 3 nodes for 10m = ~0.6 node-hours lost).
Mira: awesome. thanks everyone. I'll follow up with a short runbook to avoid manual flips during peak and add a metric for "fractional gpu fragmentation". :thumbsup:
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolled config rackWeight:100 -> 20 in rollout-canary(us-west2-a) by Ashish (ci/4567)
Mira: adding a checklist item: before changing rackWeight, run the fragmentation sim locally and check autoscaler synergy.
Devon: noted. closing thread when postmortem lands.
